evidence.claim: Defines the active initialization order from INPUT through CRACK.
Scans for INPUT and requires current type 3 before converting it to block-input mode.
Defines required/optional lookup and exact, case-sensitive matching for every requested block token.
Records the verified transition to exact SOLVER, STATISTICAL, MATERIALS, and CLUSTERS generation tokens while retaining END APPROXIMATION only as compatibility input.
Defines solver schedules and parses up to 50 current-format solver records and their options while retaining an old-format path.
Defines the case-insensitive SHEFF backend, solver, and preconditioner values accepted by the submodule revision pinned by the BSAM source commit.
Locates the optional UFUNCTIONS block and divides entries at *end records.
Normalizes each UFUNCTION entry, extracts its name and two-column numeric data, builds natural-cubic-spline coefficients, and requires strictly monotonic x coordinates.
Resolves material parameter values of the form ufunc_<name> to the first matching normalized UFUNCTION name.
Resolves interface-material parameter values of the forms table_<name>, stat_<name>_<initial>, and ufunc_<name> and binds them to the corresponding objects.
Parses MOISTURE key/value labels, resolves and checks its external environment, disables coupling on missing prerequisites, and executes the converter/program workflow.
Runs enabled moisture coupling at completed block-loading steps and applies the optional positive step-index filter.
Requires CLUSTERS, accepts solid finite-element cluster type 100, and delegates each cluster to the FE reader.
Contains the active first-five-character finite-element command dispatch and line-option handling.
Reads the last FILE option on *INCLUDE, increments the include unit, and prepends the original BSAM input directory when opening the target.
On included-file EOF, closes the current include unit and resumes the parent include or root FE stream.
Defines the DIMENSIONS, NODE, ELEMENT, NSET, and ELSET data-row grammars and next-command termination.
Defines nested integration-point records and nodal or elemental orientation records.
Requires one thickness/material row per declared layer, normalizes thicknesses, and applies the section to the selected element set.
Requires BOUNDARY and begins dispatch of boundary problem types and nested controls.
Defines mechanical/thermal problem starts and the active nested BOUNDARY command dispatch through convergence and output controls.
Defines penalty types -2/-21, nodal, and surface connection headers, subordinate set rows, defaults, sentinels, and cross-reference checks.
Defines static, fatigue, 2D-fatigue, reduced-fatigue, block repetition, and boundary-condition change records.
Defines D_AA, active four-character convergence labels, values, defaults, and the twelve-record scan limit.
Defines data-file, sum-force, volume-average, traction-average, and CFV output records and selectors.
Defines all/list/qualified-name selection for clusters and cluster-qualified node or element sets.
Requires CONSTITUTIVE, parses the common modifier prefix, dispatches every accepted constitutive record layout, and terminates entries by declaration order.
Defines constitutive record storage, the retained three-entry MIC array, and the 1,500-entry declaration-order limit.

The active finite-element initialization path resolves direct material and failure references for constitutive types 1-8 and 10 and applies *xyzload only to legacy load-vector material types 100 and 210.
Failure evaluation accepts direct types 1-8 and 10 plus interval types 11-13, while other parsed wrapper types stop; the interval selector locals are not initialized in this routine.
Locates optional TABLES and divides table entries at *end records.
Parses normalized rectangular table grids and performs label-directed bilinear interpolation with boundary clamping.
Resolves table_<name>, statistical-table, and polynomial table references from structured material parameters.
Locates the optional exact STATISTICAL start token and divides entries at *end records until END STATISTICAL DISTRIBUTIONS.
Parses statistical distribution attributes and implements active type-3 Weibull scaling for coordinate- or fiber-aligned three-dimensional seeding.
Requires MATERIALS, enumerates 28 active numeric types, parses their legacy or structured bodies, and initializes the bulk, interface, and J2 structured-material arrays.
Parses structured bulk-material key/value rows, dispatches every implemented key, and resolves constant, table, statistical, polynomial-table, and user-function parameter forms.
Parses structured interface-material key/value rows, dispatches every implemented key, and resolves constant, table, statistical, and user-function parameter forms.
Locates optional FAILURE and parses every accepted no-data, degradation-table, wrapper, CFV, and LARC04 criterion record, including interface types 34, 35, and 36.
Defines the 50-entry declaration-order FAILURE array and records the criterion families stored in it.
Dispatches bulk, interface-initiation, CFV, static, contact, and fatigue-initiation criteria using material strengths and the parser-owned failure records.
Locates optional USER and parses numeric types 1-5, 100, 101, 201, and 301 with declaration-order IDs.
Evaluates scalar analytic, piecewise, and spline USER functions and three-component type-201 curves.
Builds natural cubic splines from at least two strictly monotonic data points and evaluates scalar or three-component curves.
Defines the integer CSR-like record read by USER type 301 and assigns every stored matrix value to one.
Uses declaration-order USER function IDs from material selections to evaluate stiffness and related properties.
Locates optional CRACK, dispatches active FE crack types 101, 201, and 301, parses their shared counts, cluster, option, and predefined-crack records, and enforces count and mesh prerequisites.
Defines storage for crack parameters, normals, two failure-mode thresholds, and the 250-entry CRACK array limit.
Accepts only crack types 101, 201, and 301 in the active finite-element crack-check path and binds a crack to its referenced cluster and constitutive/failure processing.
Current project deck assembled from pre-existing mesh data using INPUT type 3, MATERIALS, CLUSTERS, and current FE commands; VTMS may have assembled or visualized the mesh but did not generate it.
Current multi-cluster project deck assembled from pre-existing mesh data that demonstrates repeated solid cluster records; VTMS may have assembled or visualized the mesh but did not generate it.

The transformed eight-ply notch deck completed input and connection setup, produced step and TP artifacts, and ran for 120 seconds before a controlled timeout stop with exit code zero and no fatal marker.

The legacy type-9 SOLVER body was migrated to current PARDISO syntax with 14 threads and an indefinite matrix; the pinned serial executable reported PARDISO, advanced through seven loading steps, and stopped cleanly after a 120-second controlled probe with no fatal marker.
Defines -I/-O directory flags, optional .in removal, basename handling, and output artifact stems.
Writes the explicit end-of-program timing sentinel after all boundary problems finish.
Defines .exit values 0 continue, 1 disrupt, and 2 stop.
A controlled copied deck produced a fatal missing-MATERIALS message while the Windows process returned exit code zero.
A controlled copied deck changed only MATERIAL to MATERIALS; its existing CLUSTERS and END CLUSTERS tokens were accepted, all steps completed, and the end-of-program sentinel was emitted.

top_level_blocks.summary: Selects the current non-sequential block input mode; the pinned executable requires type 3.

parameters.name: type
parameters.summary: Activates the current single-thread non-sequential input format before internal conversion to block mode.

variants.name: current-block-input
variants.when: the first INPUT record is type 3

fields.name: type
fields.summary: Selects the only current input format accepted by the pinned executable.

constraints: Current generation emits exactly one type record before END INPUT.
Although the reader loop can parse later type 1 or 2 records, the active main program uses only input_id 1; additional records have no current generation role.

dependencies: The first parsed type must equal 3; the parser then normalizes input_id 1 to internal non-sequential block mode.

top_level_blocks.summary: Defines one or more linear solvers and solver-specific options; defaults to serial PARDISO when absent.

parameters.name: *type
parameters.summary: Selects the current-format solver family.

parameters.name: n_threads
parameters.summary: Requests the OpenMP thread count for PARDISO/CPARDISO; values above the available maximum are capped. Current-format generation must emit this option because that path does not explicitly initialize a default.

parameters.name: matrix_type
parameters.summary: Selects the matrix classification passed to PARDISO/CPARDISO. Numeric legacy input defaults to definite; current-format generation must emit the intended value because that path does not explicitly initialize a default.

parameters.name: backend
parameters.summary: Selects the case-insensitive SHEFF backend; availability depends on how the executable was built.

parameters.name: solver
parameters.summary: Selects the case-insensitive SHEFF solver. The pinned dispatcher accepts the spellings gmes/fgmes, not gmres; none is PETSc-only.

parameters.name: preconditioner
parameters.summary: Selects the case-insensitive SHEFF preconditioner using the active parser label; ilu and ilut select the same ILUT category.

parameters.name: relative_tolerance
parameters.summary: Sets the SHEFF relative tolerance.

parameters.name: maximum_iterations
parameters.summary: Sets the SHEFF maximum iteration count.

parameters.name: petsc_opts
parameters.summary: Passes PETSc options to a SHEFF PETSc backend.

parameters.name: debug_opts
parameters.summary: Passes SHEFF debug flags; recognized flags include -pause, -write_sparsity, and PETSc-only -reorder and -save_to_binary.

variants.name: current-pardiso

fields.name: *type
fields.summary: Begins a PARDISO or MPI cluster-PARDISO definition.

fields.name: n_threads
fields.summary: Sets the OpenMP thread count; emit explicitly in current syntax.

fields.name: matrix_type
fields.summary: Sets the matrix classification; emit explicitly in current syntax.

constraints: Up to 50 current-format solver definitions are accepted.
cpardiso is replaced by pardiso with a warning in a non-MPI build.
Unknown option labels warn and are ignored.

variants.name: current-sheff
constraints: Backend, solver, and preconditioner comparisons are case-insensitive in the pinned SHEFF dispatcher.
The parser itself accepts arbitrary numeric tolerances and iteration counts; downstream solver validity is build/backend dependent.
The implementation accepts gmes and fgmes, while the source comment's gmres spelling is rejected.

variants.name: legacy-numeric
variants.when: the first record does not parse as *type

fields.name: n_threads
fields.summary: Sets threads for type 8 and is read as a dummy/thread value for type 9.

fields.name: marker
fields.summary: Selects indefinite or unsymmetric; omission retains the initialized definite default.

constraints: Accepted for compatibility and preservation diagnostics only; new solver definitions must use *type key/value syntax.
Type 9 is replaced by type 8 with a warning in a non-MPI build.
The notch_v1 deck uses this preserved legacy form.

dependencies: Solver IDs are one-based declaration order.
*SOLVER inside BOUNDARY selects the schedule that maps nonlinear iterations to declared solver IDs.
A boundary schedule 2 requires a second current-format solver definition.

top_level_blocks.summary: Defines named user functions parsed as *end-delimited entries.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: Names the function. Cleaning lowercases the header, and the semantic name is its last token after splitting on spaces, hyphens, and underscores; generation uses one unique token.

parameters.name: x
parameters.summary: Supplies the consumer-defined independent coordinate; all x values must be strictly monotonic in one direction.

parameters.name: y
parameters.summary: Supplies the consumer-defined function value paired with x.

variants.name: two-column-cubic-spline
variants.when: each entry starts with a function-name line

fields.name: name
fields.summary: Defines the function name used by ufunc_<name> references.

fields.name: *end
fields.summary: Terminates the entry and must be lowercase for the outer block splitter.

constraints: At least two numeric data rows are required.
Current safe generation emits exactly two columns; other column counts do not initialize the coefficients required by accessors.
x values must be distinct and strictly increasing or strictly decreasing.
Blank lines and commas are normalized before numeric conversion.
Leading lines beginning with * are skipped by the initializer but have no implemented semantics and are not generated.
Duplicate normalized names are unsafe because material lookup selects the first match.

dependencies: Structured material parameters may reference a function as ufunc_<name>.
Function coordinate/value units are defined by the consuming material parameter rather than by UFUNCTIONS.

top_level_blocks.summary: Configures optional coupling to the external moisture simulation workflow.

parameters.name: program
parameters.summary: Selects the lowercased moisture executable name, resolved first through the system command lookup and then as a platform executable in the moisture directory.

parameters.name: converter
parameters.summary: Selects the lowercased converter basename; the parser appends .py and requires the file in the moisture directory.

parameters.name: converter_utils
parameters.summary: Lists lowercased utility basenames; the parser appends .py and requires every file in the moisture directory.

parameters.name: directory
parameters.summary: Selects the lowercased moisture workflow directory. Safe generation uses a relative child of the input or output directory because the full-path branch is prepended with the input directory.

parameters.name: steps
parameters.summary: Selects completed block-loading step numbers at which coupling runs; omission runs at every qualifying step.

variants.name: external-moisture-workflow
variants.when: the optional MOISTURE block is present

fields.name: value
fields.summary: Sets the registered value using key = value syntax.

constraints: Generation emits one key/value pair per line even though the parser can distribute multiple keys and values around one equals sign.
Cleaning lowercases keys and values, replaces commas with spaces, removes blank lines, and compacts whitespace.
steps values must be positive because they are used as one-based array indexes.
Required environment files are <converter>.py, every <converter_utils>.py file, and mdsim.conf; the program must resolve from command lookup or the moisture directory.
Any missing directory/file/program prerequisite prints errors and disables moisture rather than stopping BSAM.
The workflow shells out to Python and the selected program, creates step directories, and moves/copies moisture outputs.
Agent execution is blocked by default until a separately trusted external-integration profile authorizes the directory, executables, scripts, and shell side effects.

dependencies: Coupling is invoked only for hygro-thermomechanical output at a completed block-loading step.
A steps list filters those invocations; no list means every qualifying step.
Execution requires the external MDSIM installation and support files and is not part of the initial notch acceptance profile.

top_level_blocks.summary: Defines one or more solid finite-element clusters and their mesh, sets, orientation, and mesh-level controls.
remaining_work: Document all command data-body grammars and element-type constraints.
Build the node/element/set/orientation dependency model required for safe ply transformations.
Classify END APPROXIMATION, which remains accepted in VTMS project exports, as a compatibility diagnostic.

top_level_blocks.summary: Defines boundary problems, loads, connections, convergence, stepping, and output controls.
remaining_work: Document every record-pair schema, allowed value, default, and dependency beneath each active nested construct.
Trace the separate contact-problem branch selected by TYPE contact.

top_level_blocks.summary: Defines constitutive law records that reference material and failure definitions.

parameters.name: type
parameters.summary: Selects a direct safely generatable finite-element constitutive record; parsed wrapper types 11-13, 21, 110, 120, and 130 are explicitly blocked.

parameters.name: material_id
parameters.summary: References a MATERIALS declaration for direct types 1-8 and 10.

parameters.name: failure_id
parameters.summary: References a FAILURE declaration for direct types 1-8 and 10.

parameters.name: mic
parameters.summary: Defines optional MIC constitutive references; the full array is retained and the second nonzero entry is the legacy primary MIC ID.

parameters.name: xyzload
parameters.summary: Marks non-mechanical load vectors as global-coordinate data for material types 100 and 210.

parameters.name: fatigue
parameters.summary: Stores a parsed fatigue criterion reference; Agent generation is blocked because no active consumer reads the stored field.

body.termination: END CONSTITUTIVE after a complete declaration

variants.name: optional-common-modifiers
variants.when: after any type line and before its type-specific data

fields.name: *MIC
fields.summary: Retains up to three MIC constitutive references.

fields.name: *fatigue
fields.summary: Stores a fatigue failure reference that currently has no active consumer.

constraints: The parser examines exactly three modifier slots; an unrecognized next record is backspaced but still consumes a slot.
Canonical generation places no more than three recognized modifier lines immediately after the type line.
*MIC matching is case-insensitive after the *mic= dispatch prefix; one value selects the first ID, while two or three values make the second ID the legacy primary and preserve the full array.
*fatigue is parsed but blocked from Agent generation until an active consumer and semantics are established.

variants.name: z-rotation-types-1-and-10

fields.name: type
fields.summary: Selects orthotropic or nonlinear orthotropic Z-only rotation.

fields.name: z_rotation_degrees
fields.summary: Fiber rotation about global Z in degrees.

constraints: Type 10 selects nonlinear orthotropic behavior but has the same input layout as type 1.

variants.name: three-axis-rotation-type-2

fields.name: type
fields.summary: Selects explicit Z, Y, then X rotations.

constraints: When no explicit element orientation is present, standardization composes X, Y, and Z rotation matrices from these values.

variants.name: tow-center-curve-type-3
constraints: Every USER reference must resolve before the orientation is evaluated.

variants.name: two-curve-interpolation-type-4

fields.name: type
fields.summary: Selects interpolation between two space curves.

constraints: All six USER references must resolve before interpolation.

variants.name: jacobian-rotation-type-5

fields.name: parametric_tow_direction
fields.summary: Selects the tow direction in parameter space.

constraints: The mesh/geometry path must provide the Jacobian orientation context.

variants.name: macro-jacobian-rotation-type-6

fields.name: type
fields.summary: Selects Jacobian rotations using macro geometry.

constraints: The referenced macro geometry must exist in the model path that supplies Jacobian orientations.

variants.name: external-orientation-types-7-and-8

fields.name: type
fields.summary: Selects external cosine-matrix orientation or COMPRO orientation.

constraints: Type 7 requires external per-element orientation data; type 8 is intended for COMPRO material type 800.

variants.name: blocked-time-step-wrapper-type-21

fields.name: step_count
fields.summary: Sets the number of referenced constitutive entries.

fields.name: label
fields.summary: Parsed but discarded row label; canonical form would equal the row index.

constraints: Parsed but blocked from Agent generation because the current active finite-element path does not call the type-21 resolver; its observed callers are deprecated paths.

variants.name: blocked-indexed-interval-types-11-to-13

fields.name: type
fields.summary: Selects X-, Y-, or Z-indexed constitutive switching.

constraints: Parsed but blocked from Agent generation because current failure/statistical consumers select with uninitialized local NX, NY, or NZ indexes.

variants.name: blocked-coordinate-interval-types-110-120-130

fields.name: type
fields.summary: Selects X-, Y-, or Z-coordinate constitutive switching.

constraints: Parsed but blocked from Agent generation because the coordinate-selection consumer is commented out and current failure/statistical consumers stop on these types.

dependencies: Constitutive IDs are one-based declaration order and are referenced by cluster assignments, sections, connections, and MIC definitions.
Every direct material_id and failure_id must resolve to existing MATERIALS and FAILURE declarations.
Types 3 and 4 require numeric USER function IDs; type 7 requires external element orientation data; type 8 is coupled to COMPRO material type 800.
*MIC entries reference constitutive IDs and may be forward references because all declarations are read before element processing.
At most 1,500 entries are stored; canonical generation reserves END CONSTITUTIVE by emitting fewer than 1,500 declarations.

top_level_blocks.summary: Defines named lookup tables used by material data.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: Names the table after the required table- prefix is removed and the entry is lowercased; generation uses a unique name without underscores for unambiguous table_<name> references.

parameters.name: row_label
parameters.summary: Labels the vertical axis. Registered labels select the corresponding material lookup coordinate; other labels retain the first positional coordinate.

parameters.name: column_label
parameters.summary: Labels the horizontal axis. Registered labels select the corresponding material lookup coordinate; other labels retain the second positional coordinate.

parameters.name: horizontal_lookup
parameters.summary: Defines horizontal grid coordinates in consumer-defined units.

parameters.name: vertical_lookup
parameters.summary: Begins each data row with its vertical grid coordinate in consumer-defined units.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: Supplies one table value for each horizontal coordinate in the row.

variants.name: rectangular-bilinear-table

fields.name: labels
fields.summary: Defines vertical and horizontal axis labels; -, /, |, and _ are accepted separators.

fields.name: horizontal_lookup
fields.summary: Defines one or more horizontal coordinates.

fields.name: value
fields.summary: Defines exactly one value per horizontal coordinate.

fields.name: *end
fields.summary: Terminates the entry and must be lowercase for the outer block splitter.

constraints: At least one horizontal coordinate and one data row are required.
Safe generation emits an exactly rectangular numeric grid; the parser only warns on row-width mismatch and may otherwise retain undefined or stale values.
Both lookup axes must be strictly increasing for deterministic lookup; the initializer assumes this but does not validate it.
Values inside the grid use bilinear interpolation, reducing to linear or exact lookup on grid lines.
Out-of-range lookups warn and clamp to the nearest boundary coordinate.
Cleaning lowercases text, replaces commas with spaces, removes blank lines, and compacts whitespace.
Duplicate normalized names are unsafe because consumers select the first match.

dependencies: Structured bulk and interface material parameters may reference a table as table_<name>.
Statistical distributions may be combined with tables, and polynomial material parameters may reference multiple named tables.
Axis and value units are determined by the consuming material parameter and axis labels.

top_level_blocks.summary: Defines named statistical distributions that modify material data.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: Names the distribution after stat-; safe generation uses one unique lowercase token without hyphens or underscores.

parameters.name: type
parameters.summary: Selects the only active generated distribution: finite-element-based Weibull scaling.

parameters.name: approx
parameters.summary: References the one-based CLUSTERS declaration whose geometry, elements, integration points, and orientation drive seeding.

parameters.name: seeding
parameters.summary: Selects global-coordinate or element-fiber-aligned seed cells.

parameters.name: seed_dimensions
parameters.summary: Uses a key exactly equal to the preceding seeding value and supplies positive seed spacing in three directions.

parameters.name: seed_window_section
parameters.summary: Required for fiber/fibers seeding and must not exceed the referenced cluster's section count.

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.summary: Sets the Weibull shape parameter.

parameters.name: v0
parameters.summary: Sets the reference volume used to scale element-seed strength.

parameters.name: generation
parameters.summary: Seeds the deterministic MKL MT19937 stream; zero selects a diagnostic dummy distribution and is not generated.

variants.name: type-3-weibull

fields.name: seeding
fields.summary: Must precede the dynamic seed-dimension key.

fields.name: <seeding-value>
fields.summary: Defines three seed-cell dimensions using a key equal to seeding.

fields.name: *end
fields.summary: Terminates the entry and must be lowercase for the outer block splitter.

constraints: Canonical generation uses stat-, type, approx, seeding, alpha, v0, and generation; accepted aliases dist-, approximation, seed, and gen are preservation/diagnostic forms.
Generation emits one key/value setting per line even though the initializer can distribute multiple keys and values around one equals sign.
The seed-dimension key is dynamic and must follow seeding because it is recognized only after seed_type is stored.
Exactly three positive seed dimensions are required by the three-dimensional array operations.
Only type 3 is implemented when generation is nonzero; other values print a not-implemented diagnostic.
generation=0 creates a 100-entry zero dummy distribution for unit testing and is not a production generation target.
Duplicate normalized names are unsafe because material consumers select the first match.

dependencies: approx references an existing one-based solid CLUSTERS declaration.
fiber/fibers mode requires a valid section and element orientations in that cluster.
Structured material parameters reference this entity as stat_<name>_<initial-value>; table and statistical references may be combined in one parameter value.
Distribution values are indexed by integration-point IDs and multiply the consuming material parameter.

top_level_blocks.summary: Defines bulk and interface material records, including current structured material forms.

parameters.name: type
parameters.summary: Selects one of the 28 active numeric material implementations; type=mises is the named spelling of type 50.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: Optional note accepted only on a key/value header such as type=mises name=steel.

parameters.name: structured_bulk_key
parameters.summary: Implemented lowercase keys for structured bulk type 999 and the shared type-50 initializer; density and tcure are aliases.

parameters.name: structured_interface_key
parameters.summary: Implemented canonical keys and aliases for structured interface type 998.

parameters.name: structured_parameter_value
parameters.summary: Material-parameter values may be constants or table_<name>, stat_<name>_<initial>, ufunc_<name>, a combined table/stat expression, and for bulk material parameters poly_<table-name>... .

variants.name: structured-bulk-type-999
variants.when: the entry header is numeric type 999

fields.name: key=value
fields.summary: Assigns bulk properties; canonical generation emits one key/value assignment per line.

constraints: The initializer lowercases and normalizes commas and whitespace before parsing.
Every assignment line must contain exactly one equals sign.
Unknown keys warn and then stop in the active dispatch; canonical generation uses only registered keys.
The advertised load_vector keyword has no dispatch case and is blocked from generation.

variants.name: structured-interface-type-998
variants.when: the entry header is numeric type 998

fields.name: key=value
fields.summary: Assigns interface properties; canonical generation emits one key/value assignment per line.

constraints: The initializer lowercases and normalizes commas and whitespace before parsing.
Every assignment line must contain exactly one equals sign.
The init alias is dispatched but omitted from the initializer's accepted-key check and therefore warns; canonical generation uses initval.
Unknown keys warn and then stop in the active dispatch.

variants.name: structured-j2-type-50
variants.when: the entry header is numeric type 50 or type=mises

fields.name: key=value
fields.summary: Assigns isotropic elasticity and J2 hardening properties through the bulk structured-material initializer.

constraints: The named header parser recognizes only type=mises or type=50 and an optional name pair.
Canonical generation restricts type 50 to the seven J2 keys even though the shared class dispatcher exposes other bulk keys.

variants.name: legacy-numeric-types
variants.when: the numeric type is any active type other than 50, 998, or 999

fields.name: records
fields.summary: Fixed or counted records consumed by the selected legacy implementation.

constraints: These 25 types are recognized and preservable, but Agent generation and field edits remain blocked until each exact record schema is documented.
Type 800 additionally reads a referenced COMPRO output file from disk.

dependencies: Material IDs are one-based declaration order and are referenced by CONSTITUTIVE records.
table_<name> and poly_<table-name>... require preceding TABLES entries with matching normalized names.
stat_<name>_<initial> requires a preceding STATISTICAL entry; when combined with a table, the table supplies the initial lookup.
ufunc_<name> requires a preceding UFUNCTIONS entry.
Changing a material type must revalidate every constitutive consumer and replace the entire type-specific body atomically.

remaining_work: Document the exact record grammar and numerical constraints for the 25 legacy numeric types.
Validate required-property sets and physical units for structured types 50, 998, and 999 before enabling material creation.
Map material-type compatibility to each constitutive and element family.

top_level_blocks.summary: Defines failure criterion records referenced by constitutive laws and damage behavior.

parameters.name: type
parameters.summary: Selects one accepted bulk, interface, contact, critical-volume, static, or fatigue criterion.

parameters.name: base_failure_id
parameters.summary: References the underlying static or surface criterion for wrapper types 22, 23, 25, 29, and 30.

parameters.name: cfactor
parameters.summary: Sets the type-26 LARC04 compression cutoff and must appear on the type line.

body.termination: END FAILURE after a complete declaration

variants.name: maximum-stress-degradation-types-1-and-2

fields.name: type
fields.summary: Selects maximum-stress degradation with ten or eleven modes.

constraints: Type 1 allocates ten failure-mode rows; type 2 allocates eleven.
Each row contains exactly eight stiffness-degradation coefficients in consumer-defined mode order.

variants.name: no-data-interface-family

fields.name: type
fields.summary: Selects an interface or cohesive criterion whose coefficients come from the referenced material.

constraints: 3=Ye interface strength; 8=V-integral surface strength; 9=cohesive surface strength; 14=Wisnom; 15-16=EVI fracture forms; 17=Davila-Camanho; 24,28,31-33=Turon variants; 34=PLIGCOE; 35=vector Turon; 36=direct Davila.
These declarations have no subordinate FAILURE records; their required strengths and fracture/fatigue data come from compatible MATERIALS and analysis controls.

variants.name: no-data-bulk-and-contact-family

fields.name: type
fields.summary: Selects a criterion with no subordinate FAILURE data.

constraints: 4=max principal stress/orientation; 45=max principal compression; 5=SIFT; 6=Hashin; 7=Gcrack; 10=maximum strain; 11=Raghava; 12=stress invariants; 13=Doyoyo-Wierzbicki; 19=strain Doyoyo-Wierzbicki; 20=LaRC03 static; 21=Camanho decohesion initiation; 27=Coulomb friction.
Applicability and required strength components are determined jointly by the criterion, the referenced material type, element/interface path, and loading mode.

variants.name: critical-failure-volume-type-18

fields.name: label
fields.summary: Parsed but discarded mode label; canonical form equals the row index.

constraints: base_failure_id must resolve and must not create a wrapper cycle.
CFV uses shared global accumulation state; executable acceptance is required for each supported parallel/execution profile.

variants.name: fatigue-initiation-wrappers-23-and-30

fields.name: type
fields.summary: Selects fatigue initiation based on a static criterion; type 30 adds strength tracking.

constraints: The base criterion must resolve and be compatible with the selected volume-failure path.

variants.name: cohesive-fatigue-wrappers-22-and-29

fields.name: type
fields.summary: Selects cohesive-fatigue propagation; type 29 adds strength tracking.

constraints: The base criterion must resolve and be compatible with the interface/MIC fatigue path.

variants.name: larc04-type-26

fields.name: CFACTOR
fields.summary: Compression cutoff factor parsed from this same line.

constraints: CFACTOR must be on the type line because the parser backspaces and re-reads that line only.
The executable initializes CFACTOR to 10 when absent, despite an adjacent source comment describing different historical defaults.
